changes: Root-caused D-A3 rather than re-tuning it. The gaze-bias state machine was already present and matched the ruling (movie lane only, isAutopilotDriving, weight 0.35, 1.5 s floor, 0.5 s release, 10 s cooldown, +25° pitch cap, walk phase only, gaze only) — but it photographed nothing, which is why the strip proved the state machine and not the crossing.

The cause: it handed solveSurfaceGaze a goal 240 m along the ST-0 ray in `travel` mode. That is ~217 m of tangential range against travel's inspectRange of 14, so `direct` was false, pitch collapsed to the seeded ±1° scan, and travel mode then clamped pitch to +15° regardless. The glance yawed toward ST-0's azimuth and never pitched up at all.

Measured before and after on the shipped solver (ch10-st0-gaze-solver-probe.ts): at 240 m/travel the solved pitch is 0.00° at ST-0 elevations of 5, 10, 18 and 27 degrees — worst error 25.00°. At the repaired 10 m proxy in `inspect` mode the solved pitch equals the capped aim exactly at every elevation, worst error 0.00°, `direct` true on every row, never above the +25° cap.

Repair: aim at a 10 m proxy ON the same ray so the solver's direct branch owns pitch, and use `inspect` mode whose ±30° band CONTAINS the ruling's +25° cap instead of silently overruling it at +15°. The cap itself is now rebuilt from the ray's own tangent at exactly the cap angle; the previous spelling clipped the up-component and re-normalized, which lands at +25.4°.

ST0_GAZE_MAX_SECONDS moved 3 -> 4.5 s, with the reason recorded inline: at weight 0.35 the shipped look-rate clamp is an exponential approach with a ~0.95 s time constant, so a 3 s window spent a third of itself in transit. The ruling's floors are untouched.
Heading, velocity, route and manual play are untouched, and the bias is still unreachable outside movie=1.

changes: S-1 and the seam still's renderCameraFov 79 are one defect, and it is a real unauthored lens move — NOT shipped feel the contract forgot to declare. FOV is not speed-coupled at all: fovTarget = 70 + 9 x boost, boost is a damped key state, resolveShipBoost is forwardHeld && sprintHeld. The 190 u/s figure is not a constant anywhere; it is a proxy for 'boost held', since unboosted terminal speed is 60/-ln(0.6) = 117.5 u/s.

And the sprint was not the player's: this run's own ch10-transit rail asserted controls.sprint = controls.forward, copied from the ch8 legs. The rail cruised at 79 and fell back to 70 only when atStandoff dropped forward — exactly the 79-at-the-seam / 70.0002-at-the-cut-line split — against a contract that declares FOV 70 throughout the transit. Suppressed in ch10-transit only.

Measured after, per beat: ch10-transit over 621 samples holds fov 70.0-70.0, boost max 0, shell scale max 1.00000, zero frames above the 73.72 threshold, and the leg still completes to done. Cost is travel time only — every trigger on the leg is distance- or state-keyed, so the seam range, standoff and hand-back are unmoved; terminal speed drops 320 to 117.5.

ch10-ask still reaches 79 with shell scale 1.17727 on 90 of 231 samples. LEFT AS IS AND FLAGGED, not overlooked: that leg is contracted as ch8 grammar reused verbatim 'by shipped vehicle state and no authored move', so its boost is shipped crossing behaviour rather than a ch10 invention. Cinematography's call.

The cockpit compensation is NOT broken: tan(fov/2)/tan(35) is applied every frame with no clamp and reproduces 1.17727 / 1.03761 / 1.00000 exactly. The sky-past-the-shell artifact is a lighting threshold — the cabin lamp sits outside the scaled shell, and the outer walls pass its 6.5-unit reach at scale 1.0708 (FOV 73.72), falling to their emissive floor and reading as a receded seat against black space. Pinning the transit at 70 removes it from this run's frames.

Seam spine arithmetic, reported explicitly because it straddles the boundary: linear 7.010 x 79/70 = 7.911 (inside 7.5-8.2); tangent-correct p/H = tan(3.505)/tan(35) = 0.087474 then 2 x atan(0.087474 x tan(39.5)) = 8.249 (marginally outside 8.2). The criterion cannot be called either way from the existing capture; after the fix the re-shot frame is at FOV 70 and needs no correction at all.
